transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Okonkwo. Thank you for coming back in to see me so quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you for seeing me. I am just... I am very troubled. I thought this was behind me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it is. This is a difficult conversation to have, and I want to be very honest with you about why your symptoms have returned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I had followed the instructions. I took every pill in that bottle.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You did. And that is where the problem lies. I made a mistake in the prescription. I prescribed the correct medicine and the correct dose, but I only gave you a ten-day supply when you actually needed twenty days to fully clear the infection.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ten days? You told me the course was complete.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was not. Because the treatment was cut short, the bacteria weren't fully gone, which is why you are feeling sick again. Does that make sense, or can I clarify anything about how the medication works?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. But it makes no sense that this happened. I have people in the community who look to me. My family... they see me struggling again. They will ask why I didn't get well. It looks as though I am failing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how much weight this puts on you. It sounds like you're worried about how this recurrence affects the way your family and your community perceive your strength and your leadership.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It is a matter of dignity.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Was it a pharmacy error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No. The pharmacy filled it exactly as I wrote it. The error was in the writing of the script. It was a failure in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you are saying it was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. There was a mistake in the duration of the treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like my time has been wasted. I spent two weeks thinking I was healthy, only to be brought back to the start.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a very frustrating place to be. I recognize that this has caused you a great deal of distress and disrupted your life.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it possible that you are sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very unfortunate situation. I wish we could have avoided this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't answering my question.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am saying that this is a regrettable outcome.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Regrettable is a word for a rainy day. This is my health.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you are feeling unheard right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know how we fix this. I cannot be sick for another month.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get you started on a new course of antibiotics immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? How do I know this one is right?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will double-check the guidelines for the full duration. You can pick up the medication today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I feel better this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should be similar to the first time, assuming we complete the full course.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you will make sure the bottle is correct?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will handle the prescription myself now.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed once.

A.justification: The resident never uses direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') and uses passive/distanced phrasing like 'regrettable outcome' when asked directly.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('worried', 'frustrating', 'unheard') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding community perception and dignity.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step (new course of antibiotics today), but fails to name a specific patient role or a prevention strategy for the future.
